correctness.rationale: For all m≥2, r_i>1,c_i>0, the scalar envelope H(N)=max_{z_i≥0,sum z_i=N}sum r_i z_i/(1+c_i z_i) is strictly increasing, strictly concave along rays and H(N)/N strictly decreasing. With A=sum(r_i+1)/c_i, B=sum sqrt(r_i)/c_i, C=sum 1/c_i, q+1/q=A/B, the vector y_i*=(sqrt(r_i)/q−1)/c_i is positive and has equal marginal derivatives q²; direct algebra gives H(K*)=K*, K*=B/q−C. For every history-dependent column-stochastic redistribution N_(t+1)≤H(N_t), yielding limsup≤K*. Rank-one D=p1^T, p=y*/K*, achieves K* from any nonzero state. Strict concavity proves K* equals sum isolated K_i iff all r_i are equal and gives quadratic rigidity of the allocation when N_t→K*. Independently evaluated exact two-patch r=(4,9), c=(1,1): q=(3−sqrt5)/2, K*=(11+5sqrt5)/2>11, equal marginal derivatives and exact growth balance. All-patch assertion is under unrestricted conservative complete redistribution only.

The sharp all-policy bound and rigidity show what any dynamic dispersal strategy can or cannot improve; the exact K* and strict-gain condition are scientifically interpretable.
